protocol_under_test: base Pi-TCP-WSL transport link only (epuck_bridge_v1); NOT the EpuckState.msg protocol (no converter exists)
bridge_variant: base (real_robot_bridge/wsl_epuck_tcp_bridge.py + pi_epuck_tcp_server.py) -- sensor-extended bridge NOT used this pilot
recorder_script_state: wsl_transport_recorder.py PRE-FIX version was used for this run: it hit a benign trailing 'rcl_shutdown already called on the given context' exception after SIGINT, matching a bug class already fixed in sequence_counter.py earlier this session. All data-critical work (CSV rows, wsl_transport_totals.json) completed successfully BEFORE that exception -- verified directly via row counts (296 valid rows) and totals.json contents. The script was patched immediately after (wraps the final rclpy.shutdown() in try/except) for future runs; this attempt's data was not discarded or re-collected because its integrity was independently confirmed.

run_window.note: main_window bounds were computed from the REAL measured overlap of Pi/WSL/bag timestamps, not a fixed offset assumption -- see the overlap-window calculation in the session record.

not_measurable: sequence_gap_count/duplicate_count/out_of_order_count/aligned_window_pdr: the currently-running BASE wsl_epuck_tcp_bridge.py does not expose the Pi's internal per-state 'seq' field on any WSL ROS topic or in /epuck_bridge/status (it is used only for internal de-duplication in _publish_latest_state, then discarded) -- there is no paired source sequence number available to compute true PDR without modifying the bridge, which was explicitly out of scope for this pilot.
not_valid: one_way_latency_ms: no cross-device clock synchronization procedure (NTP/chrony) has been run or verified between the Pi and the laptop/WSL -- wall_clock_delta_ms exists only as a clock-offset diagnostic and is never used here to compute a one-way latency. RTT (last_rtt_ms) and last_state_age_s ARE valid, because both are computed entirely within WSL's own clock (time.monotonic()/time.time() in wsl_epuck_tcp_bridge.py) and never subtract a Pi-side timestamp from a WSL-side one.
